events.headline: Nepal-Tibet Flood Death Toll Surpasses 1,100 as Nearly 4,000 Remain Missing
events.summary: The flash flood triggered by a glacial/moraine-dam collapse near Gyirong on Aug 26 sent a debris flow down about 72km of the Trishuli River corridor, destroying the Gyirong border checkpoint and dozens of settlements. The death toll has climbed past 1,100, with Nepal's government reporting 3,900-5,000 still missing; Tibet reports an additional 21 dead and about 541 missing, and UNDP estimates 2.2-2.4 million tonnes of debris.

events.headline: US-Iran Conflict Escalates: Wedding Strike Kills Five, Iran Hits Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait
events.summary: On Sept 1, the US carried out its largest strikes since the initial Larak Island exchange, hitting roughly 100 targets along Iran's southern coast including, for the first time, two Iranian oil tankers; a strike on a house in Kuhestak during a wedding celebration killed 5 people and wounded 60+, prompting Iran's Red Crescent to call for an ICC probe. Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes on US-linked sites in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait. As of Sept 4, the US has ruled out talks with Iran until ship attacks stop; no ceasefire is in place.

events.headline: Iran Fires Ballistic Missiles at US Bases in Jordan After Strike on Larak Island
events.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps launched a combined missile and drone operation against the King Hussein and Al Azraq bases in Jordan, in retaliation for a US strike on Iran's Larak Island. Jordan's armed forces reported intercepting multiple ballistic missiles; Bahrain also reported intercepting Iranian drones. The exchange marked a reignition of active US-Iran hostilities, sending global oil prices up nearly 3%.
events.locationName: Al Azraq / King Hussein Air Base, Jordan

events.headline: Canada Finalizes Retaliatory Tariffs on 700+ US Products as Trade War Escalates
events.summary: Canada is set to impose counter-tariffs of 15%-50% on more than 700 US products worth roughly $19.9 billion, effective September 8, 2026, in response to the 50% US tariffs on Canadian goods that took effect August 22. Simultaneously, Prime Minister Mark Carney moved on September 1 to ease tensions by eliminating Canada's 25% retaliatory tariffs on CUSMA-compliant US goods, while leaving sector-specific tariffs on steel, aluminum and autos in place.

events.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Tops 6,300 Cases and 3,000 Deaths as Epidemic Continues to Spread
events.summary: As of data through Sept 2, the DRC has recorded 6,342 confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) cases and 3,072 deaths, with 770 patients currently hospitalized in isolation. The latest 24-hour period saw 92 new cases across Ituri, North Kivu, Haut Uele and Tshopo provinces, with Ituri hardest hit at 5,164 cases and 2,342 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones.

events.headline: UN Security Council Briefed on Worsening Haiti Gang Violence After Kenscoff Massacre
events.summary: Following the Aug 23 Kenscoff gang massacre that killed 47 and left over 50 kidnapped and 2,600+ displaced, the UN Security Council heard briefings on worsening gang brutality in Haiti. Some hostages have been released, but a gang leader has threatened to execute remaining captives if members are killed.

events.headline: Germany Closes Russian Consulate in Bonn Over Leipzig Airport Drone Attack
events.summary: After German authorities formally attributed the Aug 4 explosive-drone attack on a Ukrainian An-124 cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport to Russian intelligence, Berlin announced it will close Russia's Bonn consulate by Sept 18 and terminate the Russian House of Science and Culture's operating contract in Berlin. Two suspects have been identified; NATO and the EU voiced solidarity with Germany.

events.headline: Sir Keir Starmer to Step Down as UK MP
events.summary: Former UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced on September 1, 2026 that he will resign as MP for Holborn and St Pancras, ending an 11-year parliamentary career, to focus on international affairs including defence, security and trade. The announcement comes roughly six weeks after he was replaced as PM and Labour leader by Andy Burnham in July 2026.

events.headline: Venezuela's Delcy Rodríguez Details $209 Billion Annual US Oil Deal
events.summary: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez publicly detailed a 25-year US-Venezuela oil agreement giving a US-led consortium 100-year rights to 17 oil fields holding roughly 65 billion barrels, with Venezuela receiving about $19 per barrel produced — an estimated $209 billion annually. Venezuela's National Assembly approved the binational energy treaty, though some opposition lawmakers criticized the lack of published terms.

events.headline: RSF Drone Strikes Devastate Power, Water and Fuel Infrastructure in Sudan's El Obeid
events.summary: Since Aug 12, RSF kamikaze drone strikes have repeatedly hit El Obeid's power station, water points, fuel stations, schools and market, alongside similar strikes on Khartoum, Omdurman and Atbara, causing severe fuel shortages of around $15 per liter and shutting hospitals and water systems for roughly half a million residents. The UN Security Council voted in September to renew Sudan's sanctions regime for another year.

events.headline: China Maintains Elevated Military Pressure on Taiwan Ahead of Possible Trump-Xi Summit
events.summary: Chinese military pressure around Taiwan remains near-constant, though somewhat reduced compared with 2024-2025 peaks, as Washington and Beijing prepare for a possible Trump-Xi summit. A reported $14 billion US arms sale package including F-16s and HIMARS remains 'in abeyance'; Trump called it a 'negotiating chip,' while Beijing warns that announcing the sale could jeopardize summit talks.

events.headline: Spain Matches All-Time September Heat Record Amid Deadliest Heat Summer on Record
events.summary: Spain recorded 45.7C in El Granado, Huelva on Sept 3-4, equaling the all-time national September record. The national health institute attributes 5,232 heat-related deaths so far in 2026, the highest since monitoring began in 2015, surpassing prior records of 4,789 in 2022 and 3,035 in 2023, amid the country's fifth heatwave and hottest January-August on record.

events.headline: Russian Drone Strikes SBU Headquarters in Kyiv for First Time in War; Injuries Rise to 12
events.summary: A Russian jet-powered drone struck SBU central headquarters in daylight on Sept 4, the first direct hit on the building since 2022. Zelensky said the drone targeted SBU chief Poklad's office; injuries were revised upward to at least 12, with 9 hospitalized and 2 in serious condition. It follows six days of intensified aerial attacks on Kyiv.

events.headline: Malta Jury Acquits Yorgen Fenech in Daphne Caruana Galizia Murder-Plot Trial
events.summary: On Sept 2, 2026, a jury acquitted Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech in an 8-1 verdict on charges of complicity in the 2017 car-bomb murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia and criminal association to commit murder. The verdict sparked outrage from her family and international press-freedom groups; the men convicted of physically carrying out the bombing remain jailed from earlier trials.

events.headline: ICE Officer Christian Castro Federally Indicted Over Minneapolis Shooting
events.summary: ICE agent Christian Castro, who shot Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis through a closed door during a January 2026 raid in north Minneapolis, was federally indicted on six counts of lying to investigators after surveillance footage contradicted his claim of being attacked. He turned himself in on Sept 3, 2026; Texas Gov. Abbott had refused to extradite him on prior state charges.

events.headline: Renewed Fighting in Somalia's Baidoa Wounds 71 as Government Battles Ousted President's Militia
events.summary: Fighting erupted before dawn on Sept 3 between Somali federal forces and fighters loyal to former South West State President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed 'Laftagareen,' with the Defense Ministry alleging al-Shabab involvement. Bay Regional Hospital received 71 wounded, including 15 women, and one civilian died before fighting stopped by early afternoon, following earlier August clashes in the same area.

events.headline: Five EU States Agree Common Model for Migrant 'Return Hubs' Outside the Bloc
events.summary: Interior ministers of Denmark, Austria, Germany, the Netherlands and Greece agreed on a common model for 'return hubs' -- offshore facilities hosting rejected asylum seekers who cannot be returned to origin countries, reportedly including Uganda and Rwanda as candidates. The goal is for hubs to be operational by 2027, with a first partner-country agreement expected around year-end.

events.headline: Kyiv Political Rift Over Wartime-Election Push Fades as Organizers Split From Fedorov
events.summary: Former official Mykhailo Fedorov's call for wartime elections in September or October triggered sustained Kyiv protests that expanded to demand ex-commander Syrskyi's dismissal, who was replaced by Gen. Drapatyi. Zelensky rejected wartime elections as something that would 'destroy' the country, and the main protest organizer subsequently also rejected the push, and the protest movement has wound down.

events.headline: Eurozone Inflation Jumps to 3.3% in August, Fuels ECB Rate-Hike Expectations
events.summary: Eurozone annual inflation rose to 3.3% in August 2026, up from 2.9% in July and the highest since September 2023, driven by an energy-price surge tied to Middle East conflict spillover. Markets have fully priced in a 25 basis-point ECB rate hike to 2.5% at the Sept 10 meeting, while underlying services inflation eased slightly.

events.headline: Japan Government Bond Yields Hit 30-Year High Amid Global Debt Selloff
events.summary: Japan's benchmark 10-year JGB yield touched 3% on Sept 1, 2026, the highest since 1996, amid a broader global bond-market selloff and concerns over PM Sanae Takaichi's fiscal plans. The 5-year yield hit a record 2.265% and the 2-year hit a 31-year high of 1.81%; household spending fell for an eighth straight month in July ahead of a Sept 3-4 30-year bond auction.

events.headline: Houthi Forces Launch Largest Ground Offensive on Hodeidah and Taiz Since 2022 Truce
events.summary: Houthi forces launched simultaneous ground assaults in southern Hodeidah and three districts west of Taiz on Sept 3, preceded by heavy artillery shelling and at least 12 ballistic missiles and drones fired at government positions, seizing positions in Taiz's Jabal Habashi district. Yemeni government media report at least 50 Houthi fighters killed or wounded in the fiercest fighting since the April 2022 UN-brokered truce, continuing into Sept 4.

events.headline: Israel's High Court Unanimously Annuls Law Shielding Ultra-Orthodox Draft Evaders From Arrest
events.summary: Israel's High Court of Justice ruled unanimously to annul a July law that had banned the IDF and police from arresting ultra-Orthodox yeshiva students evading military conscription for seven months. All nine judges found the law procedurally invalid, and eight of nine also ruled it unconstitutional as a violation of the equality principle, after the Attorney General called it an 'extreme and clear case of flawed and harmful legislation.'

events.headline: Israeli Minister Unveils Plan to Relocate Up to 1.86 Million Gazans; Strikes Continue
events.summary: Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir unveiled 'Disengagement 710,' a plan aiming to remove 250,000 Gazans within one year and up to 1.86 million within seven years via 'voluntary emigration,' citing Turkey, Ethiopia, DR Congo and unspecified Arab states as destinations. Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least 3 Palestinians in Gaza City's Rimal neighborhood on Sept 3, with the UN reporting 24 Palestinians killed over five days.

events.headline: Pakistan Monsoon Flood Death Toll Tops 100 as 1.5 Million Remain Displaced
events.summary: Pakistan's 2026 monsoon season has killed over 100 people nationwide, including 55 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and 36 in Punjab, with 2,300-plus villages affected and about 1.5 million people displaced. Punjab authorities have established over 17 relief camps in Lahore alone and 511 relief camps province-wide, with roughly 400 square kilometers under water across the Lahore and Gujranwala divisions.

events.headline: Trump Administration Misses Own Deadline on State Voter Citizenship Lists
events.summary: The Trump administration is building state-by-state citizen voter-eligibility lists under a March 31 executive order, but the DOJ told plaintiffs it will miss its own Sept 4 deadline to launch a 'Citizenship Lists Portal,' offering only 48 hours notice before launch instead. Multiple lawsuits argue the effort violates the Privacy Act.

events.headline: Australia and Pacific Nations Endorse 'Waqa Moana' Maritime Security Initiative Against Drug Trafficking
events.summary: Australia and Pacific nations unanimously endorsed the 'Waqa Moana' ('large canoe') initiative, a Pacific-led maritime security mechanism to counter transnational drug trafficking. Australia is committing about $600 million, including $49 million for AFP counter-crime programs and $312 million for Defence over ten years, plus a coordination center in Samoa and an interdiction-request body based in Fiji.

events.headline: Myanmar-Thailand Border Fighting Continues in Karen State, Displacing Thousands
events.summary: Fighting between Myanmar junta forces and Karen resistance groups has continued for about nine months along the Thai border; the junta recaptured the Mawdaung trade town in May 2026 after Karen forces briefly held it. Renewed August offensives near Myawaddy involving airstrikes, drones and artillery sent stray rounds into Thailand, forcing thousands of civilians to flee on both sides.

events.headline: Fighting Persists in DRC's Fizi and Uvira Highlands Despite M23 Doha Roadmap
events.summary: On Aug 23, the DRC and the M23-led rebel alliance agreed on a roadmap for peace negotiations under the November Doha framework, following talks in Switzerland with US, Qatari, Togolese, Swiss and AU representation. Despite this, fighting continues in the Fizi and Uvira highlands of South Kivu, including an M23/Rwanda drone strike on a Congolese coalition position on Aug 19, as a separate FARDC-allied offensive begun in January continues.

events.headline: Measles Clusters Persist in Germany While Bulgaria and Latvia Face Active Outbreaks
events.summary: ECDC data show Germany logged 59 confirmed or probable measles cases in the first 15 weeks of 2026, while Bulgaria and Latvia are experiencing active outbreaks -- Bulgaria with 102 cases in June alone and Latvia in its first outbreak since 2018, with over 40 cases already surpassing its full 2025 tally. WHO and ECDC flag declining vaccination coverage as driving the spread.

events.headline: Farage and Bardella Sign Pact Pledging to Stop Channel Migrant Crossings if Elected
events.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage and France's National Rally leader Jordan Bardella signed a memorandum at Reform's Birmingham conference on Sept 4, pledging that if their parties gain power, the UK would intercept and return Channel migrant boats to France while France would accept repatriation. Neither party is currently in government, so the pact is not current policy.

events.headline: Canada Sheds 42,000 Jobs in August, Ending Four-Month Growth Streak
events.summary: Statistics Canada reported a surprise loss of 42,000 jobs in August 2026, versus a forecast gain of 15,000, while unemployment held steady at 6.4%. The drop ends a strong April-July run that added 181,000 jobs; the public sector fell for a third straight month while manufacturing gained 22,000.

events.headline: Brazil's Ibovespa Ends 11-Session Rally as CSN Names New CEO
events.summary: Brazil's Ibovespa stock index closed at 185,188.13 on Sept 3, 2026, ending an 11-session winning streak after touching about 189,000 intraday. Separately, steelmaker CSN announced a leadership transition the same day: longtime CEO Benjamin Steinbruch moved to chairman, replaced by former Vale chief Fabio Schvartsman, sending shares higher.

events.headline: EU Defence Ministers Conclude Wicklow Meeting With Ireland Pledging EUR 125M for Ukraine Air Defence
events.summary: The informal EU defence ministers' meeting hosted by Ireland (Aug 31-Sept 1) concluded with Dublin pledging 125 million euros toward Ukraine air-defence support and training. Ukraine's Acting Defence Minister Andrii Khmara and NATO Deputy Secretary-General Radmila Shekerinska took part, with focus on missile-interceptor shortages and Russia's shadow fleet.

events.headline: Weimar Triangle Foreign Ministers Reaffirm Ukraine Support, Discuss Leipzig Drone Incident
events.summary: Foreign ministers of Germany, France and Poland met in Weimar on Sept 3-4, marking 35 years since the Weimar Triangle's founding, and pledged continued coordinated support for Ukraine and pressure on Moscow. They also discussed the Leipzig drone incident, after France summoned Russia's envoy over the attack.

events.headline: India and Belgium Sign Defense Cooperation Agreements During PM Bart De Wever's New Delhi Visit
events.summary: Belgian PM Bart De Wever made the first official visit by a Belgian premier to India in two decades, held Sept 2-4, 2026. About 10 agreements were signed covering local co-production of Thales 70mm rockets, ammunition, mine-countermeasure systems, counter-drone technology and tank turrets, plus a defense-cooperation letter of intent and a new resident Indian defense attache post in Brussels.

events.headline: Southern Ontario Continues Power Restoration After Record-Breaking Storm
events.summary: Destructive Sept 2 thunderstorms dropped over 100mm of rain on parts of Toronto, described as a '100-year storm,' downing trees and power lines and generating about 1,500 fire department calls in 24 hours. By Sept 4, Toronto Hydro had restored power to about 90% of affected customers, with 4,500-10,000 still without electricity.

events.headline: Israel Frees Five Lebanese Civilian Detainees in US-Brokered Deal, Then Raids Halta Village
events.summary: Israel released one Lebanese civilian on Sept 3 and four more on Sept 4, all confirmed by the ICRC and acknowledged by the Israeli military as civilians, in a release linked to US-mediated negotiations with Beirut over recovering remains of Jewish community leaders kidnapped in Lebanon in the 1980s. The same day, Israeli forces raided the Lebanese village of Halta and abducted three more residents, bringing the village's total to seven abducted since March 2.

events.headline: Japan Expands Defense Equipment Assistance Program to About 12 Countries
events.summary: Japan's Official Security Assistance program, launched in FY2023, will expand from 8 to about 12 recipient countries in FY2026, adding Kenya and Cambodia to existing recipients including the Philippines, Indonesia, Tonga and Fiji. The record budget of 18.1 billion yen marks the first-time provision of finished, not just dual-use, nonlethal defense equipment, linked to China's growing assertiveness in the East and South China Seas.

events.headline: Hurricane Marie Strengthens to Category 2, Lashes Baja California Sur With Rain and Swells
events.summary: Hurricane Marie strengthened to Category 2 passing offshore Mexico's Baja California Sur, about 885km WSW of Cabo San Lucas as of Sept 4, generating heavy rainfall of 75-150mm, 4-meter swells and 70km/h gusts. Classes were suspended in Los Cabos and Ciudad Constitucion, and small-vessel navigation was closed at some ports.

events.headline: Chile, Argentina, Bolivia and Peru Sign Joint Critical Minerals Declaration
events.summary: Chile, Argentina, Bolivia and Peru signed a joint declaration on strategic and critical minerals on Aug 28, 2026 at their first ministerial meeting, held in Santiago. The pact establishes working groups on geological data-sharing, oversight coordination and workforce development, leveraging the region's lithium and copper reserves.

events.headline: Anti-Immigrant Group Clashes With Congolese Refugee Camp in Durban, South Africa
events.summary: On Sept 3, hundreds of members of the 'March and March' movement confronted a camp of Congolese, Burundian and Rwandan refugees, legally verified by South Africa's Home Affairs, outside Durban's Home Affairs offices, attempting to remove their belongings. Police used stun grenades, teargas and rubber bullets to separate the groups; several people were injured, including at least four refugees hospitalized, and the group says it plans to return.

events.headline: Illegal Mining Operations Damage Critical Infrastructure Across Johannesburg
events.summary: An estimated 34,000-plus irregular 'zama zama' miners are operating in abandoned or illegal shafts across South Africa, with underground blasting in Johannesburg causing sinkholes, cracked roads and damage to electricity and water infrastructure worth billions of rand. The City of Johannesburg says it is intensifying interventions against the organized criminal networks involved.

events.headline: China Commemorates 81st Anniversary of WWII Victory Over Japan Amid Regional Friction
events.summary: China held nationwide commemorative events on Sept 3, 2026 marking the 81st anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, including a ceremony at the Nanjing Massacre memorial. China's Foreign Ministry urged Japan to 'fully remove the pernicious influence of militarism,' reflecting ongoing regional friction over Japan's defense posture.

events.headline: WHO Highlights Recurring Nipah Virus Spillover Pattern After Kerala Case
events.summary: WHO confirmed a laboratory-confirmed Nipah virus case in Kozhikode district, Kerala on June 11, 2026, with the patient hospitalized with neurological symptoms and 104 contacts identified and monitored; no secondary cases have been reported. WHO's regional office published a fresh 'expert perspective' on Sept 2, 2026 addressing the recurring, abnormal pattern of Nipah spillovers in Kerala since 2018.
